KG (KWA) ist ein gemeinsames Unternehmen des Kreises Wesel und der Stadt Kamp-Lintfort, um die zuverlässige und nachhaltig orientierte Entsorgung für die gesamte Region zu garantieren. Gegenstand dieses Vergabeverfahrens ist die Beschaffung, Implementierung, Wartung und Support einer Source-to-Pay-Lösung (eProcurement) für das Abfall- und Energiezentrum Asdonkshof. Derzeit wird SAP R/3 als Warenwirtschaftssystem genutzt. Aufgrund der fortschreitenden Digitalisierung von Prozessen und der Optimierung von Abläufen bestehen immer wieder Medienbrüche. Der Koordinationsaufwand und die Bearbeitungszeit sind damit recht hoch, weil u.a. einige Prozesse noch papierbasiert und nicht digital sind. Der unternehmensweite Geschäftsprozess von der Bestellanforderung bis zum Rechnungsausgleich soll für alle am Standort agierenden Organisationen medienbruchfrei digitalisiert und automatisiert werden, um effizienter, transparenter und kostengünstiger zu arbeiten. Die Funktionen der elektronischen Freitextbestellung (eBANF) und die Bestellung per Warenkorb durch ein Katalogangebot von Lieferanten sollen vorhanden sein. Im strategischen Einkauf werden die Funktionen Lieferantenselbstauskunft, -onboarding und -bewertung benötigt. Es wird ein Cloud-Service-Modell (z.B. Software-as-a-Service oder Managed Cloud) beschafft, damit ein bilateraler Datenaustausch mit SAP Business One reibungslos erfolgen kann. Parallel zu diesem Projekt wird SAP Business One für das Finanzwesen, Rechnungswesen, Controlling, Einkauf und Materialwirtschaft eingeführt. Für die Schnittstellen-Umsetzungen müssen enge Absprachen erfolgen. Folgende Meilensteine sind vorgesehen: Die Neueinführung der Source-to-Pay-Funktionen für Bestellanforderung, Anfragen, Angebote, Auswertung von Angeboten, Bestellung/Vertrag hat bis zum 30.06.2027 zu erfolgen ("Teil-Go Live eBanf"). Die Neueinführung der Source-to-Pay-Funktion für Lieferantenkataloge hat bis zum 31.08.2027 zu erfolgen ("Teil-Go Live Kataloge"). Die Neueinführung der Source-to-Pay-Funktionen für Lieferantenselbstauskunft, Lieferantenonboarding, Lieferantenbewertung hat bis zum 30.09.2027 zu erfolgen ("Teil-Go Live Lieferantenbewertung"). Die Neueinführung mit allen relevanten Source-to-Pay-Funktionen und Schnittstellen hat zum 01.01.2028 zu erfolgen ("Haupt-Go Live"). Die Neueinführung der Source-to-Pay Funktion für Spendmanagement hat zum 30.06.2028 zu erfolgen ("Teil-Go Live Spend"). Die Einzelheiten sind insbesondere der Leistungsbeschreibung (Anlage 1 der Vergabeunterlagen) zu entnehmen. Die Leistungsbeschreibung (Anlage 1 der Vergabeunterlagen) stellt den aktuellen Planungsstand dar, der sich im Laufe des Vergabeverfahrens und insbesondere während der Ausführung der Leistungen weiterentwickeln und verändern kann. Mit diesem europaweiten Vergabeverfahren will die KWA einen zuverlässigen, leistungsfähigen und erfahrenen Softwarespezialisten als Auftragnehmer auswählen, welcher die Implementierung, Wartung Source-to-Pay-Lösung (eProcurement) effizient und unter Beachtung des Wirtschaftlichkeitsgrundsatzes erbringt. Die KWA erwartet ein hohes Verständnis für die Ziele der KWA sowie eine lösungsorientierte Herangehensweise, um der KWA bestmögliche Ideen aufzuzeigen und diese dann umzusetzen.

title: INDUSTRY DAY: Maneuver-Short Range Air Defense Increment 4 - Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires, Portfolio Management Executive (PME) Defensive Fires
description: Description: The U.S. Government plans to host an Industry Day to provide a technical and programmatic overview of future acquisition and development opportunities for the Maneuver-Short Range Air Defense (MSHORAD) Increment (Inc) 4 program. This event builds upon the previously published Request for Information (RFI) dated March 27, 2026, under Posting ID W31P4Q-26-RFI-0001. Description: The M-SHORAD Inc 4 will be a vehicle-agnostic palletized air defense system designed to protect maneuver forces including Joint Forcible Entry (JFE) and Mobile Brigade Combat Team (MBCT) with both light dismounted and mounted maneuver operations. The M-SHORAD Inc 4 will defend against Group 1-3 Unmanned Aircraft Systems and rotary and fixed wing aircraft. The M-SHORAD Inc 4 will utilize a Modular Open Systems Approach framework and will deliver tailorable and reconfigurable sensors, electronic warfare, and kinetic defeat capabilities to warfighters. Industry Day: The purpose of this Industry Day is to provide a technical and programmatic overview of M-SHORAD Inc 4 to identify prospective acquisition and development opportunities. The primary target audience for this event includes main system integrators interested in participating in future M-SHORAD Inc 4 development and production. Subsystem and technology suppliers (e.g. sensors, effectors, motion systems or remote weapon stations, C2 ) are also welcome to attend to facilitate industry collaboration and integration partnerships. Participation and Attendance Notice: Attendance and participation in this Industry Day are entirely voluntary. Participation in any subsequent procurement, transaction, or solicitation is not contingent upon attendance at this event. The U.S. Government will not reimburse any attendees for travel, preparation, or other costs associated with participating in this Industry Day. When: 27-28 October 2026 The agenda for the Industry Day is as follows: Registration, Check-In and Badging Welcome and MSHORAD Inc 4 Overview Keynote Speaker Joint Panel Discussion and Q&A Closing Remarks and Next Steps One-on-One breakouts (pre-registration required for the 27th & 28th Oct.) Where: Von Braun Center South Ball Room�s 1 & 2 700 Monroe Street SW Huntsville, AL 35801 Registration Details: To attend this event, all interested participants must complete the registration form using the official, updated link below or QR code: no later than 23 October 2026. To ensure broad industry representation, attendance is strictly restricted to a maximum of three (3) representatives per participating organization. Link: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/9AFtEjfeuM?origin=lprLink QR code: See Attached An email confirmation will be sent by the U.S. Government verifying successful receipt of registration. Each person attending the Industry Day must provide a Common Access Card, Driver�s License, or Passport to attend the meeting. Visitors are reminded that all bags and packages brought into the facilities are subject to inspection at all times by access control personnel. Attendees should arrive at the Industry Day entrance between 0800 and 0845 on the day of the event to ensure time for check-in prior to entering the facility. title: CRMF SRF Cleanroom and UPW Construction Sources Sought Notification
description: This Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) is a Sources Sought Notice to identify General Contractors (GC) who are capable of completing the planned construction of the Cryomodule Repair and Maintenance Facility (CRMF) Cleanroom and Ultra-Pure Water (UPW) System to support the future repairs to the LCLS-II and LCLS-II-HE cryomodules. This is not a solicitation for proposal, and no award will be made from this Notice. SLAC intends to issue a formal solicitation later based on responses from this Source Sought Notice. The site for the Cleanroom install will be inside the new CRMF building and is located North of the existing Linac Sector 11, along the North Access Road, adjacent the Sector 10 Adit Road located at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, 2575 Sand Hill Rd, Menlo Park, CA 94025. This project is directly funded by the DOE's Office of Science. The DRAFT RFP package attached consists of construction documents outlining the administrative and technical specifications and drawings pending approval by SLAC�s Building Inspection Office (BIO). The final documents will be used by construction subcontractors to assist in preparing a Firm Fixed Price Proposal. PLANNED SCOPE AND DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES Base Scope (Installation of Cleanroom) The project scope includes installation of a new clean room inside an existing building, known as the Cryomodule Repair and Maintenance Facility (CRMF) building. To accomplish this task, the following specific scope elements must be completed, with all deliverable items meeting requirements as defined in the SOW. The Subcontractor is to fabricate the cleanroom per the SLAC approved design package generated by an A&E firm. The design package and Building Inspection Office (BIO) stamped print package will be supplied to the awarded Subcontractor. Option 01 Scope (UPW System) The project optional scope includes installation of a new ultra-pure water (UPW) system next to the cleanroom inside the CRMF building. SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory is seeking to award a fixed-price, turn-key construction subcontract to an experienced and highly qualified and skilled GC, to install the new Cleanroom inside the existing building, known as the Cryomodule Repair and Maintenance Facility (CRMF). The GC is required to install the new Cleanroom as detailed within the Statement of Work, Specifications, and Drawings. The GC is required to adhere to the project schedule, as outlined within the Statement of Work (SOW), while working in conjunction with SLAC to deliver the utmost safety, quality, and meet or surpass the administrative and technical requirements detailed in the Statement of Work, Specifications, and Drawings. A turn-key Fixed Price construction subcontract will be awarded to the GC who provides the best value to SLAC based on the evaluation criteria. The GC will finalize construction by performing the testing and commissioning of all new systems working with CRMF and SLAC Operations teams for a completed facility. DRAFT REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL SLAC will use a single step Best Value Trade Off selection method to identify the GC who provides the best value to SLAC based on the evaluation criteria. The Draft RFP and relevant draft references are provided to present the general scope and acquisition method for the project. The draft documents provided are subject to change and should not be construed as a solicitation. This Sources Sought Notice is NOT A SOLICITATION but instead is to identify interested vendors for the upcoming formal solicitation release. SOURCES SOUGHT RESPONSE Interested GCs with the skills, capability, workload capability, and ability to obtain bonding to complete the planned project scope are invited to submit a written response to this Sources Sought Notice. Please provide the following information: Company Name Name, telephone number, and email addresses of your company point of contact(s) who have the authority and knowledge to clarify responses. A statement of your company�s interest in receiving the formal solicitation notice and in submitting a responsive statement of qualifications. Please provide your response to Jennifer Jamison at: jjamison@slac.stanford.edu by 5:00 pm PST on Friday, October 23, 2026. SOURCES SOUGHT DISCLAIMER: Please note that any responses to this Sources Sought posting is purely on a voluntary basis. SLAC is not requesting a proposal, any pricing, or any other information that could be considered confidential or proprietary to be submitted in response to this posting or any part of this posting. Any submissions that contain pricing, proprietary information, or confidential information will be discarded by SLAC.

title: Alternative Fuels & Feedstock Initiative to Add Value to Seed Oil Crops through Improved Preprocessing, Scalability, and Valorization of Product Streams
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from prospective offerors to complement existing seed oil crop research efforts at the Biomass Feedstock National User Facility (BFNUF) through U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) funded work. Appropriate topics of research will develop a greater understanding of harvesting, storage, separations, and scalability that increase the value of seed oil crops by reducing processing costs, increasing yields, and/or generating material streams that can be valorized. Topics that are not of interest to this EOI include operations upstream of harvesting (e.g., agronomy, crop engineering, genetic engineering), and downstream of processing (e.g., new conversion technologies). This effort expects to fund a maximum of two projects through DOE�s Alternative Fuels & Feedstock Office (AFFO). Projects can be led by industry or a U.S. university, with INL collaboration. BACKGROUND AFFO and Idaho National Laboratory (INL) seek research that improves post?harvest preprocessing, storage, separations, and scalable fractionation of seed oil crops to reduce costs, increase yields, and create valuable non?oil product streams. Work must focus on post?harvest operations and demonstrate scalability. Awardees will collaborate with INL�s BFNUF and generate data supporting an INL?led technoeconomic assessment (TEA) SCOPE OF WORK BEA is seeking qualified company or U.S University to support the BFNUF and AFFO mission through novel research that increases the value of seed oil crops through more effective harvesting, storage, fractionation, and/or valorization for seed components. If the proposed work is bench-scale, a case must be made for why it is scalable to field applications. Proposed research may focus on commodity or niche seed oil crops. More niche seed feedstocks will be considered if the research team can demonstrate the extent to which the proposed methods are broadly applicable. EOIs should focus on the non-oil components of the seed, although outcomes affecting the oil extraction process can be considered in the overall potential impact of the proposed work. The winning project team will collaborate with INL and help design INL scope that uses BFNUF capabilities, which may be reviewed at Biomass Feedstock National User Facility - Idaho National Laboratory. Qualifications for successful applicants include: Technical Expertise and Leadership: Strong technical credentials and experience, demonstrated by impactful research publications. There will be a preference for teams with experience collaborating with industrial partners or in performing industrially relevant research. Collaboration and Networking: Demonstrated ability to work with and lead teams from different organizations. Industry and Workforce Development Connections: Extensive ties with agricultural companies, equipment manufacturers, and/or energy sectors. Interested applicants will propose scope to address the research challenge posed. It is anticipated that the project duration will be between 12 and 24 months and will support approximately 0.25 FTEs for project PI and 1.0 � 3.0 FTEs for technicians/post docs/students. In addition to labor, the project may include laboratory consumables commensurate with the proposed scope. Any non-consumable equipment purchases, or planned travel must be specified in the proposed scope and is subject to approval by INL. Project resources required to fund BEA and BFNUF activities are separate from the awarded amount, which will be managed through a contract with BEA. As determined by BEA, responders to this EOI may receive a Request for Proposal (RFP) that may require detailed technical and price proposals for evaluation and ranking in a selection process. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested individuals are requested to email expressions of interest to BFNUF@inl.gov and chase.egbert@inl.gov by 6PM Mountain Standard Time on October 23, 2026. Included must be sufficient written information confirming the responder�s qualifications, including the following: � For all core team members (no page limit): Name Institution Contact Information CV or Resume � A brief statement (no more than three - five pages in length) including: The objective of the planned proposed work The approach to meeting the research objective The scale and technology readiness level of the proposed work Team members, resources, and roles for each team member How the team will collaborate with the BFNUF and include an INL-led TEA Expressions of interest may be submitted by 1) Contacting BFNUF@inl.gov to receive a link to securely transmit your application using Box, or 2) Emailed directly to BFNUF@inl.gov and chase.egbert@inl.gov. If you do the latter, please enable encryption features in your email platform to ensure secure transmission. Securely sending emails protects sensitive information from unauthorized access. Transmitting PII via non-secured methods carries inherent risks for which you are accountable. Only potentially qualified offerors, as determined by BEA, will be contacted for further discussions or the release of a request for proposal for the project. Interested individuals are advised that the selection decision is anticipated in January 2027. If you have questions, need additional information, or need to speak with a BEA subject matter expert for clarification, please email BFNUF@inl.gov. For further questions regarding BFNUF capabilities, please reach out via email at BFNUF@inl.gov. Proposing teams should anticipate collecting information that will support a technoeconomic assessment completed by INL.
